description: AUTO-GENERATED FROM rules_spec.yaml. Static checklist for Review Agent.

rules.name: Strict Layered Import Flow
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan imports. Verify common/ imports no core/, engine/, or cli/; core/ imports no engine/, cli/, or rich; engine/ imports no cli/; git/ imports no other core/ package; inputs/ imports no catalog or agents; catalog/ imports no agents, sessions, engine, cli; artifacts/ imports no engine; agents/ imports no engine; sessions/ imports no agents, worktree, catalog, engine, cli. Enforced by LAYER_RULES in tests/lint/test_layer_direction.py.
rules.bad_pattern: from dovo.engine.engine import Engine  # upward import in core/sessions/

rules.name: CLI Logic Purity
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect CLI command handlers in src/dovo/cli/*/commands/. Flag direct SQL execution, domain orchestration, or business logic.
rules.bad_pattern: rows = context.db.connection.execute('SELECT * FROM worktrees').fetchall()

rules.name: Domain Fact Origin Invariant
rules.evaluation_criteria: Verify formatters only map existing fields from domain models without inventing new statuses, error categories, or domain rules.
rules.bad_pattern: if not result.git_status: result.warnings.append('Git not found')  # originates fact

rules.name: Standard Core Package Layout (Domain-Named Entrypoint)
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check package directory structure for new domains. Verify the entrypoint module is named after the domain (e.g. prune.py) rather than generic facade.py. Flag any monolithic single-file domain layout or public models defined in services/.
rules.bad_pattern: src/dovo/core/prune/ -> facade.py  # or monolithic prune.py mixing models & logic

rules.name: Secrets Environment Resolution
rules.evaluation_criteria: Search for API key field additions in DovoConfig or SQLite models. Ensure environment resolution helpers are used.
rules.bad_pattern: api_key = config.agent.copilot_token  # serializing secrets in static config

rules.name: Stateful Builder Pattern for RichOutput
rules.evaluation_criteria: Ensure core services never instantiate RichOutput or Console. Verify .print() is only called at the CLI command/orchestrator level, not inside core services.
rules.bad_pattern: output = RichOutput(); output.console.print('failed')

rules.name: Pure Layout in to_rich
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect to_rich() implementations. Flag any business logic, status calculations, or string manipulations that do not come directly from the view model.
rules.bad_pattern: color = 'green' if len(data.errors) == 0 else 'red'; return Panel(Text(color))

rules.name: Inline Error and Warning String Construction
rules.evaluation_criteria: Flag private helper functions whose sole purpose is formatting a single error or warning string.
rules.bad_pattern: errors.append(self._format_validation_error(path, err))

rules.name: Domain Shared Table Builders in common.py
rules.evaluation_criteria: When a new or changed formatter defines a table-construction helper, check whether another formatter in the same domain needs the same table shape. Flag a helper duplicated across sibling formatter modules instead of factored into that domain's common.py, and flag a domain-specific helper placed in the package-wide common.py.
rules.bad_pattern: # Nearly identical build_table() duplicated in both worktree/list.py and worktree/status.py

rules.name: Scoped Model Exceptions with Justifying Comment
rules.evaluation_criteria: Flag any model using extra='ignore' or omitting strict=True outside the approved list or without a justifying comment.
rules.bad_pattern: model_config = {'extra': 'ignore'}  # missing justifying comment

rules.name: Result/Outcome Pattern over Exceptions
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect service methods. Flag methods that raise exceptions for business/operational failures, and domain-entrypoint or command-level operations that return a plain value instead of a BaseResult. Do not flag an internal helper that returns str | None to a single in-layer caller.
rules.bad_pattern: raise WorktreeNotFoundError('Worktree does not exist')

rules.name: Reachable and Tested Status Enums
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check all enum values of StrEnum classes in models.py. Ensure each variant is emitted in src/ and asserted in tests/.
rules.bad_pattern: class PruneStatus(StrEnum): UNKNOWN = 'unknown'  # never emitted in src/

rules.name: Definition Exception Hierarchy
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect domain exception inheritance. Flag exceptions that inherit directly from Exception or ValueError instead of the Definition base hierarchy.
rules.bad_pattern: class BlueprintLoadError(Exception): """YAML syntax error."""

rules.name: Full-Word Identifiers
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect new or modified variable, parameter, attribute, and function names. Flag any name formed by dropping letters from a word, whether or not it appears in an earlier list of examples. Do not flag unmodified code.
rules.bad_pattern: val_res = validator.validate(document); acc = []

rules.name: Logical Blank Lines Separation
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check function bodies. Flag dense unseparated blocks or excessive random spacing.
rules.bad_pattern:
record = WorktreeRecord(...)
self.db.worktrees.save(record)
return result

rules.name: Terse Docstrings, Description Only for Hidden Contracts
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect new or modified docstrings. Flag a title that carries an outcome clause such as ", or why X cannot be done". Flag a description that retells the body, lists what the signature already shows, or adds no fact the title lacks. Flag a missing description where the code has a hidden contract or a safety behavior.
rules.bad_pattern: """Run the provider. First resolve the baseline, then build the prompt, then run the tool, then diff the worktree, then validate the patch."""  # or: """Return flags for the rules, or why a rule cannot be preserved."""  # outcome in the title

rules.name: Docstrings Describe Only the Documented Unit
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect new or modified docstrings. Flag a sentence that names another module's, class's, or caller's behavior, such as how an adapter handles the returned value.
rules.bad_pattern:
"""Render a restricted policy's allow and deny rules as dontAsk flags.

The adapter surfaces a returned reason as an unsupported-policy error before the process is spawned."""

rules.name: One Docstring per Unit
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect new or modified modules, classes, and functions. Flag any body with a bare string statement after its first statement.
rules.bad_pattern: """Return dontAsk flags for the rules."""  # followed by a second """...""" string statement

rules.name: Ban on -> Any Return Annotations
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan function signatures for `-> Any`. Flag any occurrence on public functions.
rules.bad_pattern: def get_payload(self) -> Any: ...

rules.name: Strict Scoping of Permitted Any
rules.evaluation_criteria: Audit Any occurrences. Flag any usage outside the four permitted boundaries.
rules.bad_pattern: def execute_step(step: Any) -> StepResult: ...

rules.name: Banned Uses of Any
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan for Any annotations that match the five banned categories.
rules.bad_pattern: proc: subprocess.Popen[Any] = ...

rules.name: Explicit ClassVar Typing for Table Names and Constants
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect SQLModel definitions. Verify __tablename__ and table constants are annotated as ClassVar[str].
rules.bad_pattern: __tablename__ = 'worktrees'

rules.name: Precise Parameterization for Generator Types
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan typing annotations for `Generator[...]`. Verify all three parameters are specified (e.g. `Generator[YieldType, SendType, ReturnType]`).
rules.bad_pattern: def get_session() -> Generator[Session]: ...

rules.name: Scoped Pyright Suppressions With Reason
rules.evaluation_criteria: Grep changed hunks for `# type: ignore` and `# pyright: ignore`. Flag every bare `# type: ignore`. For each `# pyright: ignore[...]`, verify a one-line reason is present and that the case matches one of the three permitted categories; flag any suppression of `reportCallIssue`, `reportArgumentType`, or `reportIncompatibleVariableOverride` that does not match its named exception.
rules.bad_pattern: queue: Queue = mock_queue  # type: ignore  # bare ignore, suppresses nothing and hides a fixable fixture type

rules.name: Expose Public Query Properties
rules.intent: Protects a class's freedom to change its internal representation. Callers learn its state through a public interface, so a refactor stays local instead of breaking every caller that reached inside.

criteria.question: Is every access to an underscore-prefixed, non-dunder member in src/dovo/ made on self, cls or mcs rather than on another object?
Does each class that callers query for boolean state expose that state as a public property?

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Is every access to an underscore-prefixed, non-dunder member in src/dovo/ made on self, cls or mcs rather than on another object? 2. Does each class that callers query for boolean state expose that state as a public property?
rules.bad_pattern: if runner._process is not None: ...  # caller inspecting private state

rules.name: No Test Seams in Production Signatures
rules.intent: Keeps production signatures free of dead code written for tests. Every parameter exists because a production caller needs it, so the public surface reflects real behavior and tests do not shape production APIs.

criteria.question: Is every parameter, kwarg or callback with a default value in a new or modified function in src/dovo/ passed by at least one production caller?

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Is every parameter, kwarg or callback with a default value in a new or modified function in src/dovo/ passed by at least one production caller?
rules.bad_pattern: def run(self, cwd: Path, _runner: GitRunner | None = None) -> RunOutcome: ...  # only tests pass _runner

rules.name: No Ad-Hoc DB Instantiations in Loops
rules.evaluation_criteria: Detect repository or DovoDb instantiations inside for/while loops or inside reusable helper functions.
rules.bad_pattern: for item in items: repo = SessionsRepository(path); repo.create(item)

rules.name: Database Migration Hygiene and Consumer Call Sites
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check Alembic migrations. Verify added columns/tables are actively queried and written by production services in the same PR.
rules.bad_pattern: # Migration adds column future_flag with zero callers in src/

rules.name: Indexed Column Queries vs O(n) In-Memory Lookups
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan for in-memory list comprehensions or filter loops over full table fetches when an indexed query method could be used.
rules.bad_pattern: record = next((r for r in repo.list() if r.path == relative_path), None)

rules.name: Sibling Repository CRUD Method Naming Consistency
rules.intent: Sibling repositories name the same operation with the same verb, so a caller who knows one repository can use the others without reading each class, and a divergent name reads as a different behavior.

criteria.question: Does every repository class that inserts a new record expose that operation as a public create() method?
Does every repository method that returns at most one record looked up by its identifying key have the name get?
Does every repository method that returns a collection of records of one entity have the name list?
Does every repository method that removes a record have the name delete?
Does every repository method that persists changes to a whole existing record have the name save?
Does every repository method named insert, add or upsert have a docstring or comment stating why a canonical verb does not fit?
Do all repository classes that expose the same non-CRUD operation give it the same method name?

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Does every repository class that inserts a new record expose that operation as a public create() method? 2. Does every repository method that returns at most one record looked up by its identifying key have the name get? 3. Does every repository method that returns a collection of records of one entity have the name list? 4. Does every repository method that removes a record have the name delete? 5. Does every repository method that persists changes to a whole existing record have the name save? 6. Does every repository method named insert, add or upsert have a docstring or comment stating why a canonical verb does not fit? 7. Do all repository classes that expose the same non-CRUD operation give it the same method name?
rules.bad_pattern: CostsRepository.record_token_usage(...) inserting a CostRecord while sibling repositories use create()

rules.name: Consistent Error Semantics Across Queries
rules.intent: Query paths that read the same data report bad rows the same way, so a caller never mistakes a silently swallowed failure in one path for an empty result while a sibling path reports it.

criteria.question: Does every query method that reads an entity report an invalid enum value or corrupt row, by raising or by returning a BaseResult error, whenever a sibling query method that reads that entity reports it?
Does every except block in a query method re-raise or convert the caught error into a BaseResult error, instead of returning None or an empty value?

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Does every query method that reads an entity report an invalid enum value or corrupt row, by raising or by returning a BaseResult error, whenever a sibling query method that reads that entity reports it? 2. Does every except block in a query method re-raise or convert the caught error into a BaseResult error, instead of returning None or an empty value?
rules.bad_pattern: list() raises on a row with an invalid status while get() returns None for the same row

rules.name: Shared Repository Transaction Logic in BaseRepository
rules.intent: Transaction handling for repository writes lives once in BaseRepository, so commit, rollback, deletion and session behavior stay identical across repositories and a fix is made in one place instead of in every sibling.

criteria.question: Does every repository method that persists a record commit through BaseRepository._commit?
Does every repository method that deletes a single record delete it through BaseRepository._delete_where?
Is the rollback after a failed commit written only in BaseRepository?
Does every repository method obtain its session from BaseRepository.session()?
Is every other transaction block shared by two or more repository classes defined once in BaseRepository?

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Does every repository method that persists a record commit through BaseRepository._commit? 2. Does every repository method that deletes a single record delete it through BaseRepository._delete_where? 3. Is the rollback after a failed commit written only in BaseRepository? 4. Does every repository method obtain its session from BaseRepository.session()? 5. Is every other transaction block shared by two or more repository classes defined once in BaseRepository?
rules.bad_pattern: session.add(record); session.commit()  # in a repository subclass

rules.name: Redundant Index Declaration on Unique Columns
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect SQLModel Field definitions. Flag fields specifying both `unique=True` and `index=True`.
rules.bad_pattern: session_id: str = Field(unique=True, index=True)

rules.name: Released Migrations Are Immutable and Reversible
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check the diff for changes to revision files that exist in the latest v* tag. Verify every new revision defines downgrade(), avoids PRAGMA and sqlite_master, and has upgrade and downgrade tests in tests/core/db/test_migrations.py.
rules.bad_pattern: # Editing 0001_initial_schema.py after v0.6.0, or a revision whose downgrade() is `pass`

rules.name: Atomic File Writes via Temporary Sibling
rules.intent: Config and state files are never left half-written, because they are written atomically instead of in-place.

criteria.question: Is every write to a config or state file made through Filesystem.atomic_write_json or Filesystem.atomic_write_text?
Is every config or state file write free of a direct open(..., 'w') call?
Is every config or state file write free of a direct Path.write_text call?
Does each atomic write helper write to a .tmp sibling of the target and swap it into place with Path.replace?
Does each atomic write helper flush and call os.fsync on the temporary file before swapping it into place?

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Is every write to a config or state file made through Filesystem.atomic_write_json or Filesystem.atomic_write_text? 2. Is every config or state file write free of a direct open(..., 'w') call? 3. Is every config or state file write free of a direct Path.write_text call? 4. Does each atomic write helper write to a .tmp sibling of the target and swap it into place with Path.replace? 5. Does each atomic write helper flush and call os.fsync on the temporary file before swapping it into place?
rules.bad_pattern: with open(config_path, 'w') as f: json.dump(data, f)  # hypothetical in-place write

rules.name: Advisory Cross-Process Locking
rules.intent: Concurrent dovo processes must not corrupt shared worktree, catalog or state data, so mutations are serialized by the shared advisory workspace lock and a failure to obtain it is reported rather than ignored.

criteria.question: Is every worktree, catalog or state mutation that can run in more than one process at once performed while holding the .dovo/.lock advisory lock?
Is the lock acquired through WorkspaceLock from common/lock.py?
Is LockTimeoutError handled where the lock is acquired or by a caller that reports it?

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Is every worktree, catalog or state mutation that can run in more than one process at once performed while holding the .dovo/.lock advisory lock? 2. Is the lock acquired through WorkspaceLock from common/lock.py? 3. Is LockTimeoutError handled where the lock is acquired or by a caller that reports it?
rules.bad_pattern: self.lifecycle.create(...)  # hypothetical: mutates the shared .dovo directory without acquiring the lock

rules.name: Strict Public-Only Backwards Compatibility
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect PR diffs. Flag breaking renames to CLI options, config keys, or published JSON outputs.
rules.bad_pattern: # Renaming user CLI option --timeout to --wait without alias

rules.name: Ban on Internal Compatibility Shims and Aliases
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan internal classes for deprecated aliases or shim properties.
rules.bad_pattern:
def _unlock_fd(self): ...
_unlock = _unlock_fd  # internal shim alias

rules.name: Greenfield Architecture Default
rules.evaluation_criteria: Flag dual implementations or fallback branches created without an explicit issue requirement.
rules.bad_pattern: if config.use_legacy: return LegacyLoader().load()  # unnecessary compatibility branch

rules.name: Test at Contracts, Not Implementation
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect test assertions. Flag assertions checking internal mock call counts or private attributes.
rules.bad_pattern: assert service._internal_cache_size == 1; assert mock_parser.call_count == 1

rules.name: 1:1 Source Parity Layout
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check every test file path against its source module using the fixed mappings. Flag part-numbered or grab-bag files (for example test_command_formatters_part1.py or a single test_<command>.py holding more than one command action), a CLI command test file left flat under tests/cli/ instead of nested under its own tests/cli/<command>/ subdirectory, missing __init__.py files, and source modules with no test file.
rules.bad_pattern: tests/cli/commands/test_worktree_create.py  # flat under tests/cli/commands/, not nested under tests/cli/worktree/

rules.name: Standardized Test Naming and Vague Name Ban
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check test class and method names against the banned list and naming pattern.

rules.name: CLI Tier Matrix and Handler Test Necessity
rules.evaluation_criteria: For each command action, verify at least one runner integration test exists and covers the scenario classes: exit 0, option and argument binding for every declared option or flag, non-zero exit, --format json, and interactive flows if present. A command action with no *RootTests suite is not itself a violation. Flag *RootTests whose assertions duplicate an expected result object already asserted in tests/core/.
rules.bad_pattern: class ConfigShowRootTests: ...  # pass-through handler re-asserting the ConfigLoadResult from tests/core/config/

rules.name: Formatter Presentation Contract Protocol
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect each formatter test file. Flag missing wire-format boundary cases, model_dump comparisons standing in for a literal dict, identity view aliases added to satisfy the count, and render assertions on labels or layout rather than view values.
rules.bad_pattern: ErrorPanelView = ErrorPanelEvent  # alias so an identity transform can be asserted

rules.name: Parameterization-First for Sibling Variations
rules.evaluation_criteria: Flag copy-pasted or near-identical sibling test methods differing only by input parameters or expected outcomes. Scan test bodies for `for item in items:` loops over test cases.
rules.bad_pattern: def test_eval_model(self): ...; def test_eval_dict(self): ...  # duplicate sibling methods

rules.name: Assert Domain Invariants on Results; Pin Schemas in Dedicated Contract Tests
rules.intent: Protects tests that fail only when behavior breaks. Assertions target the domain outcome under test, and model shapes and defaults are pinned once in contract tests, so unrelated changes do not break scenario tests.

criteria.question: Does every field assertion in a scenario test check a field that carries the scenario's domain outcome rather than an incidental envelope field or default?
Does each scenario or integration test of a specific behavior or error condition use targeted field assertions instead of whole-model equality?
Does each new or modified model with defaults or a serialization contract have a dedicated contract test in tests/common/ or tests/core/*/test_models.py that asserts them?
Are model shape, default values and serialization asserted only in dedicated contract tests rather than in scenario or integration tests?
Does each model have at most two dedicated contract tests?
Does each test of a wire payload with a published schema contract, such as a CLI JSON formatter, verify the exact wire payload?
Does each test avoid faux-matchers such as ANY_TIMESTAMP and ANY_UUID where their only purpose is to satisfy whole-object matching on database records or unowned system state?

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Does every field assertion in a scenario test check a field that carries the scenario's domain outcome rather than an incidental envelope field or default? 2. Does each scenario or integration test of a specific behavior or error condition use targeted field assertions instead of whole-model equality? 3. Does each new or modified model with defaults or a serialization contract have a dedicated contract test in tests/common/ or tests/core/*/test_models.py that asserts them? 4. Are model shape, default values and serialization asserted only in dedicated contract tests rather than in scenario or integration tests? 5. Does each model have at most two dedicated contract tests? 6. Does each test of a wire payload with a published schema contract, such as a CLI JSON formatter, verify the exact wire payload? 7. Does each test avoid faux-matchers such as ANY_TIMESTAMP and ANY_UUID where their only purpose is to satisfy whole-object matching on database records or unowned system state?
rules.bad_pattern: assert result.status == WorktreeDiffStatus.NOT_FOUND; assert result.error_code is None; assert result.warnings == []; assert result.fixes == []  # incidental defaults in a not-found scenario

rules.name: Test Double Realism and Production Types
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect test doubles and stubs. Verify they inherit from production types or satisfy typing.Protocol.
rules.bad_pattern: class MockAdapter: def __getattr__(self, name): return MagicMock()

rules.name: Ban on Negative Existence Tests for Deleted Symbols
rules.evaluation_criteria: Grep for `assert not hasattr` in tests/. Flag any occurrence.
rules.bad_pattern: assert not hasattr(filesystem, 'old_helper')  # negative existence test

rules.name: Complete Assertions Invariant
rules.evaluation_criteria: Flag tests where the sole check is `assert result is not None` or redundant `isinstance` checks.
rules.bad_pattern: assert result is not None; assert isinstance(result, RunOutcome)

rules.name: Determinism and Clock Virtualization
rules.evaluation_criteria: Grep for time.sleep in tests/. Permit occurrences inside the shared harness poll helper only, and flag every open-coded poll loop or bare sleep in a test module. Flag subprocess-spawning tests that do not register with the process registry.
rules.bad_pattern:
while time.monotonic() < deadline:
    time.sleep(0.05)  # open-coded poll loop in a test module

rules.name: Rich Render Width Pinning
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan for console render captures and ensure render_rich with width=160 is used. Flag ambient-width captures, and flag render assertions whose expected string is a caption or label rather than a value taken from case.view.
rules.bad_pattern: assert 'Session ID' in rendered  # panel caption, changes with layout and pins no contract

rules.name: No Sole Consumer Tests
rules.evaluation_criteria: Verify every touched production function has a real caller in src/. Verify every harness symbol has at least one caller outside tests/harness/. Flag harness verification suites that exhaustively permute options no domain test uses.
rules.bad_pattern: # StepBuilder.with_retry() exercised only by tests/harness/test_builders.py

rules.name: Strict Typing on Test Helpers and Fixtures
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect type annotations in tests/helpers/ and fixture functions. Flag missing types or MagicMock in signatures.
rules.bad_pattern: def create_test_session(db: Any, mock_obj: MagicMock) -> Any: ...

rules.name: Orchestration Path Test Coverage
rules.evaluation_criteria: Verify that PRs modifying command routing or multi-step orchestration include a test exercising the updated execution branch.
rules.bad_pattern: # PR modifying Engine.resume() without integration tests for resumed step loop

rules.name: Public Function Happy and Unhappy Path Coverage
rules.evaluation_criteria: For each public function or method in a changed production module, verify its corresponding test file (per TEST-002) contains at least one test exercising a success path and at least one test exercising a failure or boundary path. Flag any public function with only happy-path tests, any dedicated test method targeting a private (underscore-prefixed) function, and any public function with zero covering tests. Trivial properties (single field return, no branch) require only a happy-path read.

rules.name: CLI Runner Assertion Boundary
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan each CLI command domain's test directory under tests/cli/<command>/ for containment or equality checks against stdout or rendered output; any literal assertion, including a snapshot comparison, is permitted. Flag only assertions against help text wording, and name the Click metadata check that should replace them.
rules.bad_pattern: assert "Show the current configuration value" in result.output  # help text wording; assert Click metadata instead

rules.name: Test Layer Import Boundary
rules.evaluation_criteria: Scan import statements in changed files under tests/core/. Flag any import of dovo.cli or a submodule of it.
rules.bad_pattern: from dovo.cli.worktree.commands.prune import prune_command  # imported from tests/core/worktree/test_prune.py

rules.name: Command Result DTO Spy Scope for CLI Integration Tests
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect any dispatch-spy fixture use under tests/cli/. Verify every assertion made against a captured item is an instance of that command action's own declared Result type. Flag an assertion against any other dispatched event type captured by the same spy, and flag spy[0]/len(spy) == 1 relied on without isolating the command's own Result type for a command action that can plausibly dispatch more than its terminal result in the same invocation.
rules.bad_pattern: assert isinstance(dispatch_spy[-1], MessageEvent)  # asserting an incidental progress event through the result spy

rules.name: Test-Layer Docstrings Are Terse Contracts Without Tags
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect new or modified docstrings under tests/. On a test method, flag a docstring that carries a tier tag, opens with a non-imperative word, exceeds 120 columns, or only rewords the test name. On any other unit, flag a title that carries an outcome clause or lists steps, a description that retells the body, restates the signature, or adds no fact the title lacks, a sentence describing another unit's behavior, and a bare string statement after the docstring.
rules.bad_pattern:
"""[tier-3/integration] dovo worktree create: 3 prior worktrees exist -> exit 1, 'Maximum active worktrees reached' in stdout."""
"""Give the provider's winning credential 'test-token', patch a finished-stream runner, and return both."""  # helper: lists steps and restates the return type

rules.name: Architecture Doc Structural Gate
rules.evaluation_criteria: Verify diff in docs/agents/architecture.md only modifies structure sections (layers tree, package boundaries), and only when a package is added, removed, or moved or an import boundary changes. A new boundary also needs a row in LAYER_RULES in tests/lint/test_layer_direction.py.
rules.bad_pattern: # 100 lines of narrative prose explaining pruning heuristics in architecture.md

rules.name: User-Visible Behavior Documentation Scope
rules.evaluation_criteria: Verify new CLI options or behavioral changes are documented in docs/cli/.
rules.bad_pattern: # Documenting user CLI flag --keep-on-failure inside architecture.md

rules.name: Schema and Entity Documentation Gate
rules.evaluation_criteria: Verify schemas.md changes only when a stated contract changes, and flag schemas.md edits that add field lists, enum members, exception names, or method lists.
rules.bad_pattern: # Listing a new Result model's fields in schemas.md

rules.name: Ban on Duplicating Source in Docs
rules.evaluation_criteria: Flag doc changes that copy-paste field lists or enum members from source models without adding context.
rules.bad_pattern:
| Field | Type | Default |
| session_id | str | required |

rules.name: Unavoidable Spec Tables Require Parity Tests
rules.evaluation_criteria: Verify every specification table in docs has a named automated test under tests/lint/ asserting parity, and resolve the named path to a file that exists. Flag manual tables of CLI flags or schema fields with no parity test, and flag doc sentences naming a parity test that is absent from the tree.
rules.bad_pattern: # "enforced by tests/lint/test_doc_parity.py" where that module is nowhere in the tree

rules.name: Prefer Deletion Over Accretion
rules.evaluation_criteria: Review doc edits for conflicting old vs new statements.
rules.bad_pattern: # Appended new rule while leaving old formatters.py text intact

rules.name: Canonical Terminology Invariant
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check doc prose and code comments for terms the Terminology table does not define, or defined terms used outside their meaning (e.g. calling a session a 'run').
rules.bad_pattern: 'A session executes the blueprint.'  # the act of executing is a run; the session is what it leaves behind

rules.name: Verifiable Doc and Rule Claims
rules.evaluation_criteria: For each doc claim of the form "enforced by", "gated by", or "see <path>", resolve the path. For each documented helper or fixture name, resolve the symbol. Flag unresolvable claims, rule examples naming nonexistent modules, and doc paragraphs describing behavior absent from the tree. For each docstring in the diff, and each docstring of a function whose behavior the diff changes, re-read it against the code and flag any sentence the change made false.
rules.bad_pattern: # "enforced by tests/lint/test_doc_parity.py" in AGENTS.md, where the module does not exist

rules.name: Pre-Commit Quality Suite Gate
rules.evaluation_criteria: Verify `dovo run quality` succeeds before any commit. Verify the fail_under value in pyproject.toml is greater than or equal to the previous committed value. Flag any PR that lowers fail_under, and flag test additions whose stated justification is raising coverage.
rules.bad_pattern: # fail_under lowered so a commit can pass, or tests added purely to reach a percentage

rules.name: Git and Pull Request Attribution Hygiene
rules.evaluation_criteria: Inspect commit message trailers and PR descriptions. Flag AI co-author trailers.
rules.bad_pattern:
feat: prune worktrees

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursor@cursor.sh>

rules.name: Agentic Process State Declaration
rules.evaluation_criteria: Check agent turns prior to tool execution for stated directive and scope. Flag tool execution lacking state declaration as advisory warning.
rules.bad_pattern: Running write_to_file without stating governing directive or target scope

rules.name: Mechanical Enforcement Parity
rules.evaluation_criteria: For each BLOCKER rule, identify its executing check or its explicit review-only classification. Verify invariant checks include a regression test matching the suite's real shape, such as assertions inside a *Tests class rather than a module-level function. Flag configuration that disables a declared gate and allowlists that grew.
rules.bad_pattern: # Scanner walks only tree.body functions, so class-based tests are never inspected
